title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from p.70). f: X -> S is a smooth curve with a section t, and X* = X \ t(S). X' -> X is finite, with X' smooth of relative dimension 1 over S. It has a section t' over t and is tamely ramified of index n along t'. This means that étale-locally X' is the Kummer cover O_X[z]/(z^n - phi). Here n is not assumed invertible. The Kummer description gives a canonical isomorphism (2), kappa_{t'}: T_{X'/S,t'}^{otimes n} -> T_{X/S,t}, between tangent line bundles along the sections.

This page. Let G be a finite étale group scheme over S. Suppose G_{X*} acts on X'* = X'|X* making it a G_{X*}-torsor (marginal NB).
- The stabilizer G_{t'} of the section t' (the inertia group scheme) is a subgroup scheme of G.
- G_{t'} acts faithfully on the line T_{X'/S,t'}, giving a monomorphism G_{t'} -> Aut(T_{X'/S,t'}) = G_{m,S}.
- Its image lies in mu_{n,S}, because the action on T^{otimes n} = T_{X/S,t} is trivial. In the Kummer model the inertia is exactly mu_n.
- Inverting G_{t'} = mu_n yields a canonical monomorphism (3), mu_{n,S} -> G. This is the canonical inertia generator at the cusp, without any choice of root of unity.

Separately, with f° = f|X*, the torsor X'* defines a class (4), xi in H^0(S, R^1 f°_* f°*(G)). This is the torsor class locally on S.

Proposition. The datum (X', t', G-action) is determined up to unique isomorphism by (3), (4) and (2). The next page makes this precise as a functor between two categories:
- the triples (X', t', G);
- the systems (G, n, xi, i: mu_n -> G, T, k: T^{otimes n} -> T_{X/S,t}).

Why this is plausible:
- X' is recovered as the normalization of X in the torsor X'*.
- t' is pinned down (up to normalizer action) by the inertia embedding.
- T = T_{X'/S,t'} together with k rigidifies the remaining central automorphisms, so isomorphisms become unique.
- The local-on-S class xi glues because of this rigidity.

Purpose. This is the relative (over a base S) local theory of tame G-covers near a marked section, with tangential data. It is the ingredient for 'épi-groupes de revêtements' and for tangential base points in the study of moduli of elliptic curves and the Teichmüller/Galois tower.
errors: Tension with the p.70 caveat that n is not assumed invertible. If G is finite étale and X'* is a G-torsor, then mu_n embeds in G, which is étale; this forces mu_n to be étale, i.e. n invertible on S (at least where ramification is nontrivial). Equivalently, an inseparable Kummer cover cannot be an étale torsor on X*. So in this G-torsor setting the 'n not invertible' generality is vacuous.
'Gom_S' in the formula is G_{m,S}. The phrase 'l'image dans ... -> mu_{n,S}' is elliptic: what is meant is that the faithful character identifies G_{t'} with mu_{n,S}, and (3) is the inverse map.

The proposition as stated ('(3), (4) and (2)') is incomplete as a reconstruction statement. One also needs T with an identification T = T_{X'/S,t'} (supplied on the next page) to obtain uniqueness of isomorphisms; otherwise central elements of G in mu_n act as nontrivial automorphisms. Also xi in H^0(S, R^1 ...) only determines the torsor locally on S, so the gluing relies on that rigidity.

ideas.what: Canonical inertia embedding mu_n -> G at a tame branch point, obtained from the faithful action of the stabilizer on the tangent line.
ideas.modern_name: canonical inertia character / cyclotomic form of the branch-cycle datum; banding of the gerbe at a marking of a twisted G-cover
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA1 XIII, tame ramification); Fried and Serre (branch cycle argument); Abramovich–Corti–Vistoli (twisted G-covers, 2003)
ideas.where_published: Tame ramification and the tangent-space character are in SGA1 XIII (Grothendieck–Murre); the canonical mu_n -> G formulation is unsure.

ideas.what: Isomorphism T_{X'/S,t'}^{otimes n} = T_{X/S,t} and data (T, k), i.e. an n-th root of the tangent line at the marked section.
ideas.modern_name: tangential base points; root stack / twisted curve marking; log-structure root
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989) for tangential base points; Cadman and Abramovich–Graber–Vistoli for root stacks/twisted curves
ideas.where_published: Tangential base points are alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this relative formulation is unsure.

ideas.what: Classification of pointed tame G-covers of (X, t) over a base S by (G, n, xi, i, T, k).
ideas.modern_name: local structure of the stack of twisted/admissible G-covers (balanced twisted stable maps to BG); Hurwitz stacks with marked ramification

missed.claim: Around 1980–82, Grothendieck formulates the relative (over arbitrary S) classification of tame G-covers at a marked section. The data are: a canonical mu_n -> G inertia embedding, a local-on-S torsor class, and an n-th root T of the tangent line at the section. This is essentially the data later encoded by twisted G-covers / root stacks (ACV, Cadman), here phrased without stacks.
missed.quote: d'où un monomorphisme canonique (3) mu_{n,S} -> G ... (X',t') ... est défini à isomorphisme unique près par la connaissance des (3) (4) et de (2)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority for the cyclotomic, choice-free inertia datum combined with tangential rigidification over a base, used in the Grothendieck–Teichmüller setting. It is mathematically subsumed by later theory.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, early relative formulation of tame G-covers with tangential rigidification, anticipating twisted-cover/root-stack descriptions. However, the content is standard tame ramification theory in modern terms, and the unique-isomorphism claim needs the extra datum T supplied on the next page.
